themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 15 THIS WEEK versus a 5.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 161% increase—signaling a sudden outbreak of pavement hazards affecting pedestrian safety across Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 15 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (161% spike, z-score: 5.18)
Spike appears isolated to current week with no prior sustained trend in data
Aligns with community board's long-standing requests for enhanced infrastructure and street-level maintenance
reporting_angles: Ground truth reporting: walk affected blocks to document specific hazards and interview residents about trip/fall incidents
Interview DOT and 311 about what triggered the spike and response timeline

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Suddenly Failing
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints exploded to 7 complaints 3 weeks ago from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 5500% spike (z-score: 20.79)—indicating either a storm event, disease cluster, or delayed reporting of neglected street trees in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 complaint weekly average (5500% increase, z-score: 20.79, highest z-score in dataset)
Extreme statistical anomaly suggests discrete event (storm damage, pest infestation, or maintenance failure) rather than gradual trend
Community board budget requests mention parks expansion, suggesting longstanding tree/green space concerns
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints correlate with a specific weather event or pest issue (e.g., emerald ash borer)
Interview Parks Dept on tree inventory status and removal/replacement timeline in Bed-Stuy

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste & Lot Blight
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped 178% LAST WEEK (17 vs. 6.1 weekly average) and lot condition complaints spiked 1500% (4 vs. 0.2 weekly average), together suggesting emerging sanitation and blight crisis affecting residential blocks.
evidence: Residential disposal: 17 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.1 weekly average (178% spike, z-score: 11.73)
Lot condition: 4 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 5.67)
Two distinct sanitation categories spiking simultaneously suggests systemic waste/cleanup issue, not random complaints
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific blocks with clustered complaints to identify common triggers (e.g., missed pickups, illegal dumping, squatting)
Contact DSNY on collection schedule changes or staffing shortages affecting Bed-Stuy

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Going Missing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.1 complaint weekly baseline—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—potentially indicating organized theft, neglect, or a hidden public safety issue with wayfinding.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Extreme spike from near-zero baseline suggests concentrated incident (theft ring, vandalism campaign, or data reporting error)
Pattern mirrors sidewalk condition spike, both pointing to deteriorating street infrastructure
reporting_angles: Verify via ground reporting whether signs are actually missing or just a reporting artifact
If real, investigate whether NYPD has theft reports or if DOT recognizes a vandalism pattern

themes_detail.label: Stray Bikes & Property Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked 860% LAST WEEK (6 vs. 0.6 weekly average, z-score: 7.72) alongside unsanitary animal complaints on private property (967% spike, 4 vs. 0.4 average), signaling potential homelessness, encampment, or squatting activity.
evidence: Abandoned bike complaints: 6 LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score: 7.72)
Unsanitary animal (private property) complaints: 4 two weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Two proxies for encampment/vacancy activity spiking in close timeframe; aligns with community board's homeless services budget requests
reporting_angles: Canvass specific blocks with clustered complaints to identify encampments, vacant buildings, or informal settlements
Contact DHS and NYPD Outreach to map recent activity and available resources in Bed-Stuy
